chunk_map.heading: Phase 2: Mark the line you trust least
Phase 4: Ask it the other way round

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L51: 'Then ask, of each person's digest in turn' / L47 'your four lines' resolves to the four named in L27 (chunk 1) and re-listed in L51; L21 'the door your team agreed on Day 1' resolved by L33 'the door in `team/what-goes-in.md`, or your brief'. Closest: L76 'each tied to a line and a source' resolves to the doubts of Phase 2/5. Session artifacts (digest, brief, bet) are exempt carve-out. Harm (unresolved referent on a wall) absent.

L27 'the two lines you wrote into the brief on Day 1, what to look for and what you expected' names the source by claim and unpacks it in the same sentence; no 'the opening lecture' style positional pointer (grep above/below/top of page: only L72 'top of `team/doubts.md`', a file, not page geometry).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L27 Day 1 look-for and expectation lines: curriculum/exercises/apt101-send-it-off.md and apt101-write-the-bet.md exist (ls); maintainer L90 names producers. L33 'the door in team/what-goes-in.md' consumed from Day 1 per L90.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L51 'Laptops half shut.' is a verbless stage direction, but L51 continues 'Each of you reads your four lines to the other two' (verbed instruction); no guess-before-reveal beat exists and no outcome is narrated above a guess. L60-64 phase 4 asks for no prediction.
Shortest chunk, chunk 5 (L66-72): 'Together, pick the one doubt that matters most for the bet... That is a team call, not a vote' is a self-carrying claim.
Closest: chunk 4 'Phase 4: Ask it the other way round' (L56) is true to L60 'run your digest once more... with only your look-for line turned round'. Headers are phase labels; bodies match.

Closest: L39 'Every line in it came from your material. You know these sources. The agent read them once.' is three sentences with different subjects/content, not anaphora or a verb triplet with an empty leg. L41 'Not the one that is plainly wrong; the one you would least want...' is a single contrast, not 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'. No superlatives, no number+retraction, no abstraction stacks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nEi '\b(below|above|beat|surface|firing|compendium|mood|forcing function)\b' on body L1-77 -> only L72 'top of' (file location). Door, brief, bet, doubt, look-for line are the training's own earned vocabulary per L21 and Day 1 exercises, not repo dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L13 bolds three UI labels '**Overnight digest**', '**Routines**', '**Run now**' (each <=2 words, UI control names, no whole-sentence bold); plus widget labels '**Session**', '**What you do:**'. Harm (whole-lead-sentence monoculture) absent; handle cap held.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: exercise file with only ## phase chunks included whole by modules; no phase-less prose section; check-slide-size reports 6 slides

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js -> 'OK — 55 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' exit 0; headers Phase 1..5 consecutive (L23,35,47,56,66); in-body ref L13 'Phase 1' resolves.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js -> 'OK — 55 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.'; prompt-body 'below' is inside a fence in the same chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no links or in-body anchors in body (has_urls false)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/apt101-read-the-digest.md -> 'slides: 6 ... oversized: 0'; no accept-note needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise headings are phase labels (L23 'Phase 1: See what ran' ... L66 'Phase 5: Pick the doubt') and L74 'Take stock'; no declarative heading needed or present; no claim requirement binds a label walk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L76 'The digest read more than any of you could. Each of you still knew one source well enough to catch where it went past what was there.' is a closer recap, but it adds the exercise's takeaway (reading where you know most) not stated as doctrine earlier in the body; L52-53 two bullets are the two questions asked aloud. L45 'If your doubt lands on a typo, look again.' is a move, not a kicker.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: git log -p -3 -- file | grep '^[+-]## ' -> no ## header change in recent commits; no provenance note of a rename in maintainer block.

notes: Only accept-note in maintainer block is the Quality line (no rule-specific attestation). Prompt fences (L9-11 and expanded registry prompts) exempt. Body-view slide_count 6 excludes the title chunk.
